## What does this PR change?

<!-- One or two sentences. -->

## Type of change

- [ ] Correction — fixing an outdated version, renamed concept, dead link, or claim that is no longer true
- [ ] Official protocol resource — spec, changelog, official SDK, governance document, reference implementation
- [ ] Independent analysis — vendor-neutral write-up explaining or comparing protocols
- [ ] Protocol-level developer tool — validator, conformance checker, inspector
- [ ] Something else (explain below)

## Why does this belong in this list?

<!--
Answer the scope test from CONTRIBUTING.md:

  Does this help someone UNDERSTAND OR IMPLEMENT a protocol,
  or does it OFFER THEM A SERVICE that uses one?

"It uses x402 / MCP / UCP" is not by itself a reason — that describes most of
the software being written right now.
-->

## Affiliation

- [ ] I have **no** affiliation with the project or company being added
- [ ] I am **affiliated** with it (employee, founder, contractor, or paid to promote it)

<!--
Affiliated submissions are welcome if disclosed and if they pass the scope test —
in practice, open-source protocol infrastructure rather than a hosted service.
Undisclosed affiliation discovered during review is grounds for declining on its own.
-->

## Checklist

- [ ] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] Every link in this PR resolves (I checked, rather than assuming)
- [ ] Version numbers, product names, and protocol concepts are current as of today
- [ ] The entry format matches the surrounding entries: `- [Name](url) - Description`
- [ ] No emoji markers, pricing, performance claims, or superlatives in the entry
- [ ] The entry is placed in an existing section — I have not added a section to house it
- [ ] Any figure I cite is stated consistently throughout
- [ ] This is my only open PR against this repository
